reason: Execution workers refuse a project table seen only inside a subquery or bare EXISTS. has_entity_with_metadata (first use of every command approval), engagement_has_dependents (DELETE of a non-archived project) and Butler search's private-chat filter used that shape and failed in supervisor mode. They now select a mapped id with LIMIT 1, and Butler search outer-joins the chat on its primary key so the guard scopes it. New worker regression tests in test_execution_scope_probes.py (sqlite and PostgreSQL, using the execution fixture) cover both probes, the fenced answer for another project's approval, and a crafted document that names another project's chat. The other selected suites cover the same helpers and search outside workers: storage and guarded-delete semantics, session record lookups, federated search, the read-responsiveness search path, and Butler's private-chat search contract.
exclusions: test_butler_administration.py is selected only for its two search tests: its starter-template tests ([skill], [agents_md]) fail identically on pristine origin/main. Playwright area project-deletion matches storage.py but is excluded: its fixture (tests/v3/application_model_fixture.py) crashes at startup on main since the async store change (un-awaited store.create), and it runs a single-process Core that never had the worker guard. The supervisor-mode journey was checked on a scratch Postgres Core instead (DELETE of a project with a chat: 500 on main, 409 'archive it instead' on this branch; Butler search_resources tool: CoordinationConflict on main, results on this branch). No UI, native or frontend code changed. PostgreSQL variants run only where NEBULA_TEST_POSTGRES_URL is set.
